text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm drafting a follow-up to the onboarding RFC. Thinking about splitting the pipeline into ingest -> fast-smoke -> deep-bench as independent services. Main Q: should compatibility/validator checks live in ingest (fail-fast) or in fast-smoke (more context)?

javier: my +1 for split responsibilities: lightweight invariants in ingest, heavier checks in fast-smoke. ingest should avoid long-running ops.

sasha: Concern: if ingest only does tiny checks we risk surface mismatch across environments. We should standardize a contract spec so both stages share the same rules.

lin: Agreed with sasha. Proposal: ingest enforces a "manifest sanity" surface (tokenizer, model shape, signature), fast-smoke runs behavioral regressions + perf smoke. Keep fullbench run async.

maya: yes — failure modes: 1) ingest rejects due to malformed weights 2) smoke flags tokenization drift 3) deep-bench finds quality regression. We need clear classification and ownership.

javier: ops cost note — running even a tiny smoke for every push increases GPU churn. Can we do probabilistic sampling + immediate deterministic sanity?

sasha: sampling is fine for perf/quality; but compatibility (abi/tokenizer) must be deterministic on every ingest. Otherwise host apps hit 500s.

lin: Pseudocode for manifest we discussed:
```
model_manifest:
  name: string
  tokenizer: { type: "hf", rev: "1.2.0" }
  shapes: { layers: int, hidden: int }
  checks: ["tokenizer_roundtrip", "kv_shape", "signature_match"]
```
That keeps ingest cheap: run a few pure-Python checks + binary header parse.

maya: good. For adapter/quantization variants, can we attach variant descriptors rather than re-running heavy checks for each quantized binary? e.g. inherit pass/fail from base + lightweight runtime check.

javier: yes — variant descriptors + a compatibility matrix. If base fails, all variants fail. If base passes, variants get a short runtime quickcheck (1-2 inferences) that uses cached golden inputs.

bench-bot: queued fast-smoke job 8382 for model: gpt-slim-v2 (trigger: ingest-4920001111)

sasha: On sampling: define sampling policy per org/priority. PLG models get more frequent deep-bench; background contributors get probed. That keeps cost sane.

lin: On reproducibility: fast-smoke must store seeds + environment (torch/cuda) in bench artifact. We should record kernel selection and quant flags so rollback is possible.

maya: Good point — bench artifacts should include: manifest, seed, runtime-env, golden-responses, and a small diff summary. That helps triage regressions.

javier: Interface boundary idea: ingest exposes a 1-liner API: POST /models {manifest, weights_ref} -> returns {status: accepted, intake_id}. Then fast-smoke subscribes to intake events with intake_id and decides scheduling based on policy.

sasha: That decouples them nicely. Also lets us put an admission window: if fast-smoke backlog high, route to canary pool.

lin: Edge-case: tokenizers that depend on model-generated vocab (we saw this with a custom SentencePiece). ingest can't fully validate tokenization without model load. For those, mark manifest flag `requires_live_load: true` and route to synchronous fast-smoke pre-accept.

maya: agree — add `requires_live_load` boolean with explicit owner approval. automation: an RBAC gate to prevent accidental slow accepts.

javier: small ops ask — surface approximate cost estimate in ingest response so teams see expected bench cost (e.g., "fast-smoke ~0.1 GPU-min"). Helps avoid surprises.

sasha: +1. Also include suggested quantization / batch configs from Optimize service for cheaper runs.

maya: Next steps: I can write a short RFC addendum describing interfaces + manifest schema. lin can sketch the manifest JSON schema, javier will draft sampling policy options, sasha will enumerate failure categories and owner mapping.

lin: will push manifest schema draft by EOD.

sasha: I'll enumerate owner mapping and RBAC requirements tomorrow.

javier: I'll do sampling policy + cost-estimate fields.

maya: Perfect — thanks. ping me if you want a short pairing session to finalize the manifest fields. :thumbsup:
